extracted.intended_audience: prospective NSF proposers (principal investigators), institutional proposal administrators, and research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Official NSF Part I (Chapter I) guidance on preparing and submitting proposals: describes allowed submission systems, types of funding opportunities, submission types (concept outlines, LOIs, preliminary proposals, full proposals), eligibility, registrations, deadlines, required proposal content, and processing timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed proposal submission systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless specified in an NSF program solicitation, proposals submitted to NSF must be submitted via Research.gov, Grants.gov, or the Broad Agency Announcement Management (BAAM) System.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the system specified by the program solicitation when it modifies the general PAPPG provisions. Research.gov supports preparation, submission, updates, and budget revisions. Grants.gov submissions must follow the NSF Grants.gov Application Guide. BAAM usage and policy will be provided in the relevant solicitation or BAA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research.gov submission capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Research.gov may be used for proposal preparation, submission, proposal file updates, and budgetary revisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The policy and procedural guidance contained in Part I of the PAPPG pertains to proposals submitted via Research.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: FastLane decommissioning / transitional support
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal Preparation and Submission in the NSF FastLane System is being decommissioned; during transition some parts may remain open to support review and limited updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal file updates and budget revisions can be made for FastLane-submitted proposals for a limited period only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of funding opportunities: Program Descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Program descriptions are broad descriptions of programs and activities used to encourage proposal submissions to specific NSF program areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They utilize generic eligibility and proposal preparation instructions in Part I and the NSB-approved merit review criteria. See Chapter III for review criteria details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of funding opportunities: Program Announcements
rubrics_metrics.description: Program announcements are formal NSF publications that announce NSF programs and use the generic PAPPG instructions and NSB merit review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the generic Part I guidance unless the announcement states otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of funding opportunities: Program Solicitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Program solicitations encourage submission in specific program areas, are generally more focused and time-limited, and typically define competition among proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A solicitation may (and when it does, must) modify PAPPG Part I provisions (e.g., add review criteria, require LOIs or preliminary proposals, restrict proposer categories, limit proposals per organization/PI, require cost sharing, limit F&A, specify award/reporting conditions, anticipate cooperative agreements). Follow solicitation-specific instructions when present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of funding opportunities: Broad Agency Announcements (BAAs)
rubrics_metrics.description: BAAs are broad funding opportunities used for basic and applied research, focusing on advancing science rather than acquiring specific products; NSF may fund BAA responses as grants, cooperative agreements, contracts, or other arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BAAs are broad in subject matter; see FAR Part 35.016 for additional information and follow the BAA-specific instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of funding opportunities: Dear Colleague Letters (DCLs)
rubrics_metrics.description: DCLs provide general information, clarify/amend policy, or inform about upcoming opportunities or special competitions (including RAPID, EAGER, RAISE, conferences, supplements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DCLs may announce interest in proposals for specified topical areas or competitions; follow any instructions contained in the DCL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept Outline requirement and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Some proposal types or funding opportunities may require a Concept Outline prior to a full proposal. A Concept Outline is a concise summary containing info about prospective PI(s), NSF organizational unit(s), project title, keywords, and brief narrative descriptions of the idea and fit to special criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary purposes: determine appropriateness for proposal type/funding opportunity and reduce administrative burden. Concept Outlines are considered by program officers; proposers will receive email indicating whether a full proposal may be submitted. Full proposals submitted without required Program Officer Concurrence Email will be returned without review or not accepted. Concept Outlines may be submitted by email or via ProSPCT; follow the funding opportunity's directions on formatting and submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: ProSPCT requirements for Concept Outlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The ProSPCT webform uses drop-down selections, validations, and text-entry fields with character-count limits to ensure minimal complete information and consistent formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ProSPCT users must have a valid Login.gov account. Use the specified fields and limits so the submission can be properly identified and considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Intent (LOI) usage and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Some solicitations require or request LOIs in advance of full proposals; an LOI is not binding and is used to gauge competition and help avoid conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An LOI normally contains the PI’s names, proposed title, list of possible participating organizations, and a one-page synopsis describing the work sufficiently for reviewer selection. Collaborative projects must submit a single LOI for the entire project. LOIs are submitted electronically and failure to submit a required LOI will result in a full proposal not being accepted or returned without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary proposals: purpose and submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Some solicitations require or request preliminary proposals to reduce unnecessary effort when success chances are small, increase full submission quality, and assist program staff in managing review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary proposals are prepared via Research.gov’s Proposal Preparation Module; the PI selects 'Preliminary Proposal' on the Cover Sheet and completes only required sections. The AOR signs and submits via NSF electronic systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary proposal decision types: Invite/Not Invite
rubrics_metrics.description: Invite/Not Invite decisions are final and affect eligibility to submit a full proposal; only invitees of favorably reviewed preliminary proposals may submit full proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF will electronically notify the PI and the organization's SPO of invite/not-invite decisions. Full proposals submitted without an invite when required will be ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary proposal decision types: Encourage/Discourage
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage/Discourage decisions are advisory only; both favorably and unfavorably reviewed preliminary proposers remain eligible to submit full proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF will notify PI and SPO of the encourage/discourage decision; proposers may still submit a full proposal regardless of decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full proposal required content elements
rubrics_metrics.description: A full proposal should present: (1) objectives and scientific/engineering/educational significance; (2) suitability of methods; (3) qualifications of investigator and recipient organization; (4) effect on infrastructure of science, engineering, and education (if applicable); and (5) amount of funding required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal should clearly present intellectual merit and broader impacts and be prepared with the care and thoroughness of a paper submitted for publication. Provide sufficient information for reviewers to evaluate the proposal according to the NSB's two merit review criteria (see Chapter III).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of scholarship and attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF expects strict adherence to rules of proper scholarship and attribution; authors other than the PI/co-PI must be named and acknowledged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serious failures (fabrication, falsification, plagiarism) can result in research misconduct findings and NSF action; OIG investigates allegations and refers completed investigations to NSF. Research misconduct policies are discussed in Chapter XII.C and 45 CFR Part 689. Prepare all parts of the proposal with equal care for attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement to use the Metric System
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers are encouraged to use the Metric System (SI) in proposals; recipients are encouraged to use metric units in reports and correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This encouragement aligns with the Metric Conversion Act of 1975 and E.O. 12770 (1991).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may submit proposals: general encouragement and nondiscrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF welcomes proposals from all qualified scientists, engineers, and educators and strongly encourages women, minorities, and persons with disabilities to participate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF complies with Federal statutes and policies prohibiting discrimination; some programs may have special eligibility requirements that limit eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of eligible proposers (IHEs, non-profits, tribal governments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible organizations include accredited U.S. Institutions of Higher Education (IHEs), non-profit non-academic organizations (museums, observatories, research labs, societies), and tribal governments as defined by statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program solicitations may impose more restrictive eligibility. Special instructions apply when funding international branch campuses of U.S. IHEs (justify benefits and why activities cannot be performed at U.S. campus and check the appropriate Cover Sheet box).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and conditions for for-profit, state/local, and foreign organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: For-profit U.S. organizations, state and local governments, and foreign organizations may be eligible under specified conditions or solicitations; NSF rarely provides direct funding to foreign organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsolicited for-profit proposals may be funded for special national concern or exceptionally meritorious work; US affiliates of foreign orgs must contact the program officer. Foreign orgs can participate with funding requested only for U.S. portion unless justified (unique expertise, facilities, access, or significant education/training benefits)—such justification must be in the project description and the Cover Sheet box checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Federal Agencies and FFRDCs: limited eligibility and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Other Federal agencies and FFRDCs do not normally receive NSF support, but under unusual circumstances they may submit proposals if they meet specific exceptions determined by a cognizant NSF Program Officer in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include special projects with unique contributions, national/international programs where NSF bears responsibility, and international travel awards for agency staff when needed. Contact the program officer prior to preparing proposals under these exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unaffiliated individuals ineligible for direct NSF funding
rubrics_metrics.description: Unaffiliated individuals in the U.S. and unaffiliated U.S. citizens are not eligible to receive direct NSF funding support; they must affiliate with an organization that can meet 2 CFR §200 requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals submitting NSF Postdoctoral Fellowship solicitations are not considered unaffiliated for that program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission timing: target dates, deadline dates, submission windows
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF uses target dates (proposals still accepted after date), deadline dates (proposals after date not accepted/returned), and submission windows (periods when proposals are accepted and whose end date converts to deadline policies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must be received by 5 p.m. submitter's local time on the established deadline date (including LOIs and preliminary proposals). If a deadline falls on weekend/holiday it is extended to next Monday/business day. Failure to submit by 5 p.m. local time results in non-acceptance. Target dates, deadlines, and windows are published on NSF website and in solicitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special exceptions to deadline policy (natural/anthropogenic events)
rubrics_metrics.description: Flexibility in meeting deadlines due to natural or anthropogenic events may be granted with cognizant Program Officer approval; generally up to five business days extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request authorization as early as possible; to submit after the deadline proposers must check 'Special Exception to the Deadline Date Policy' on the Cover Sheet and upload a statement identifying the nature of the event under Nature of Natural or Anthropogenic Event in Single Copy Documents. If available, upload written program officer approval under Additional Single Copy Documents. NSF handles cases on a case-by-case basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special exceptions to deadline policy (NSF closure)
rubrics_metrics.description: When NSF is closed due to inclement weather or other reasons that interfere with ability to submit, deadlines that occurred during closure are automatically extended to the following business day after closure ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This policy does not apply to closures due to lapses in appropriation; different guidance will be issued in those cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate or substantially similar proposals prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: The same work/proposal cannot be funded twice; submission of duplicate or substantially similar proposals concurrently to more than one program may result in return of redundant proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple programs should review, more than one program may be designated on the Cover Sheet; nonetheless redundant concurrent submissions will be returned. See Chapter IV.B for additional duplicate submission policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized Organizational Representative (AOR) certifications at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: In submission of a proposal, the AOR is required to provide certain NSF-specific proposal certifications; submission of government-wide representations and certifications is addressed via SAM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification occurs concurrently with proposal submission; see Chapter II.C.1.d for listing of required certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: UEI and SAM registration requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposers must provide a Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and must have a valid and active SAM registration to use NSF electronic systems and submit proposals; NSF will validate UEI/SAM prior to allowing submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registration is not active or not revalidated annually, submission and award approval actions will be blocked. Subrecipients must obtain a UEI and register in Research.gov but need not be registered in SAM; GSA provides a process for subrecipient-only UEI issuance without full SAM registration. Organizations are responsible for maintaining and updating SAM registration; NSF uses SAM as the system of record for organizational info (legal business name, physical address) and cannot override SAM data/statuses. Reactivation can take 3–5 business days after IRS validation of Tax ID when registering.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAM registration maintenance and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: SAM registration must be renewed and revalidated at least every 12 months and must include recertification of government-wide financial assistance representations and certifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to renew/maintain SAM registration will impact submission, processing, award approval, and receipt of payments; lapsed registration takes longer to reactivate if not current when revalidated.

rubrics_metrics.name: NSF ID requirements for individual users
rubrics_metrics.description: The NSF ID is a unique numerical identifier assigned to users by NSF and used across NSF systems; each individual should not have more than one NSF ID.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users with more than one NSF ID should contact the Help Desk for assistance. SSNs are requested only when necessary for business purposes (e.g., financial reimbursement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal receipt, tracking, and communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Once submitted, PIs can check proposal status via NSF electronic systems; if a proposal number does not appear, contact the Help Desk. Communications should be addressed to the cognizant NSF Program Officer with reference to the proposal number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposers are strongly encouraged to verify submission status via NSF systems and use the proposal number in all communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal processing and award timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers should allow up to six months for programmatic review and processing; the Division of Grants and Agreements generally makes awards within 30 calendar days after program division/office recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants/cooperative agreements to organizations that have not received NSF awards in five years, involve special situations (coordination with another agency or private funder), cooperative agreements, or unusual arrangements may require additional review and processing time. Time-sensitive proposals (e.g., conference/group travel) will be accepted for review only if received sufficiently in advance to permit award processing. Until an award is made, NSF is not responsible for any incurred costs.
